## Claims
- [source-backed] In type \(A_{n-1}\), the paper states that one can produce smaller generating sets for \(I_w\) and \(J_v\), conjecturally minimal for \(J_v\), and work over \(\mathbb Z\). [source-2, lines 922-929]
- [proved] Let \(A=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}A_d\) be a nonnegatively graded ring and \(F\) a homogeneous generating family of a nonzero graded ideal \(J\). If \(f\in F\) is nonzero and \(\deg g>\deg f\) for every \(g\in F\setminus\{f\}\), then \(f\) is indispensable: every element of the ideal generated by \(F\setminus\{f\}\) has zero degree-\(\deg f\) component.
- [proved] For either family
  \[
  \{\;s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\;\},\qquad
  \{\;s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\;\},
  \]
  the member \(s_{i^j}\) is indispensable provided its image in \(H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\) is nonzero. Indeed, it has degree \(ij\), while every other indexed partition strictly contains \(i^j\) and hence has degree \(>ij\); apply the preceding claim.
- [proved] If
  \[
  a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)=0\quad\text{or}\quad b=\min(i,j)=0,
  \]
  then each displayed family is the singleton \(\{s_{i^j}\}\), since both upper bounding partitions equal \(i^j\). Consequently, under the accepted contextual assertion that these singleton families generate a nonzero \(J_v\), both are minimal.

## Strategy
Use the grading to establish irredundancy generator-by-generator. The unique least-degree Schur generator is already forced. A full proof would require analogous obstructions for every \(\mu\supsetneq i^j\), equivalently nonvanishing independent classes in \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\).

## Gaps
- The argument proves indispensability only of \(s_{i^j}\), not of the remaining \(\binom{a+b}{a}-1\) generators.
- Nonvanishing of \(s_{i^j}\) in the relevant quotient was not independently grounded in the supplied excerpts.
- No supplied evidence yields the necessary lower bound
  \[
  \mu_{\mathbb Z}(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v)\ge \binom{a+b}{a}.
  \]

## Next
Construct explicit degreewise relations for \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\), then seek functionals or mod-\(p\) quotients separating every indexed \(s_\mu\).
